sections.h2: What are the options for selling a house in St. Joseph, MO?
sections.html:
A St. Joseph owner can sell through an agent, sell without one, or take an as-is offer from a cash buyer. Which one fits depends on how the house looks, how fast you need to close, and what the local market will pay.

That last point deserves attention, because St. Joseph prices differ from the rest of this group. The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 median for owner-occupied homes here is $154,200, against $197,500 in St. Louis city and $298,700 in St. Charles. At lower price points, a few thousand dollars in repair costs or agent fees takes a larger bite out of what you walk away with, which is why many owners compare a net figure from each route before deciding.

  • Agent sale: broad exposure, with commissions and closing timelines set by the contract and the buyer's lender.
  • Owner sale: lower cost, but you carry the marketing and the paperwork.
  • Cash sale: the buyer takes the house as is and you choose the closing date within reason.

sections.h2: What kind of city is St. Joseph for a home seller?
sections.html:
St. Joseph is the seat of Buchanan County, on the Missouri River in the northwest corner of the state, about 30 miles north of Kansas City. Joseph Robidoux, a fur trader, founded it, and it was incorporated in 1843. Wikipedia says it was the westernmost point reachable by rail until after the Civil War, and that it was an endpoint of the Pony Express from April 1860 to late October 1861. Outlaw Jesse James died here, and the city's slogan reflects both.

The downtown grid carries the names of Robidoux's children, including Faraon, Jules, Francois, Felix, Edmond, Charles, Sylvanie and Messanie. The city covers 44.04 square miles of land and has a 26-mile parkway system with an urban trail, anchored by Krug Park on the north and Hyde Park on the south. Corby Pond, Lake Contrary and the riverwalk add to the outdoor options.

Population has been slipping slowly: the Census Bureau puts the mid-2025 estimate at 71,001, down 2.0% from the 2020 base. Both St. Louis and St. Joseph are losing residents, so pricing a house realistically matters more here than in the growing suburbs to the east.

sections.h2: What work and schools keep buyers in St. Joseph?
sections.html:
Manufacturing and health care anchor the local economy. According to Wikipedia, St. Joseph has the third-largest manufacturing economy in Missouri, after St. Louis and Kansas City. A 2019 list of employers names Mosaic Life Care at 2,922 workers, Triumph Foods at 2,400, the St. Joseph School District at 1,635, the 139th Airlift Wing of the Missouri Air National Guard at 1,114, and Boehringer Ingelheim Vetmedica at 1,070. Missouri Western State University enrolls more than 3,800 students.

Most of the city lies in the St. Joseph School District, which operates three public high schools (Benton, Central and Lafayette), four middle schools and 16 elementary schools. A small piece of the city belongs to the Mid-Buchanan County R-V School District. Shopping is concentrated along North Belt Highway on the east side, including East Hills Mall, and two interstates, I-29 and I-229, connect the city to Kansas City and Council Bluffs. Wikipedia notes plans to replace the downtown portion of I-229 with a surface boulevard, a project that may affect houses near the corridor.

sections.h2: Does St. Joseph have rules for rental houses and inspections?
sections.html:
Yes. The city runs a Residential Rental Certification Program that began in July 2019 and requires rental units to pass a minimum code inspection every five years. If the house you are selling is a rental, the certification matters to a buyer who plans to keep it rented.

The city's application materials list an inspection fee of $50.00 for each inspection performed by a city inspector, and rentals also need a business license. Forms go to the Housing Compliance Inspection Office, 1100 Frederick Avenue, City Hall Room 107.

  • Business license for rental units: online application.
  • Unit Certification Application and Consent of Entry forms.
  • Residential Rental Unit Inspection Checklist, which shows what inspectors look for on the exterior and interior.
  • Tenant Complaint Form, useful to know about if a tenant has raised concerns.

Ask the Housing Compliance office whether your address has a current certificate before you list or sign a contract. The city's rental pages do not describe an occupancy inspection tied to selling an owner-occupied home, so check with the city to see whether anything applies to your parcel.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about St. Joseph housing?
sections.html:
St. Joseph has the lowest home values and rents of the four cities in this group, along with a high poverty rate. The table shows the main QuickFacts numbers.

sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Buchanan County?
sections.html:
Deeds for St. Joseph property are recorded with the Buchanan County Recorder of Deeds at 411 Jules Street, Room 103, St. Joseph, MO 64501. The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the phone number is 816-271-1437. No documents are recorded after 4:00 p.m. on a business day; anything presented later is recorded in the order received starting at 8:00 a.m. the next business day.

The recorder states that it cannot make out deeds or answer legal questions, and recommends retaining an attorney or title company. For fees, call the office, since the amounts depend on the document and page count. A title company normally records the deed and collects fees at closing, so you will see the charge on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: How do river and weather conditions affect St. Joseph houses?
sections.html:
Wikipedia describes a humid subtropical climate bordering on humid continental, with nearby stations typically reporting 12 to 20 inches of snow a year. The airport sits low, near the Missouri River, and its winter lows run several degrees colder than elsewhere in the city. Streams and water bodies include Roys Branch, Whitehead Creek and the river itself.

If your house is near a creek or the river, gather any elevation certificate, flood insurance records and repair receipts for your buyer. Asking neighbors and the city about drainage problems before you list helps you answer questions truthfully, whether your buyer is financing or paying cash.

faqs.q: What is the typical home value in St. Joseph, Missouri?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists $154,200 as the median value of owner-occupied housing units for 2020 to 2024. Median gross rent is $898.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed after selling a St. Joseph house?
faqs.a: At the Buchanan County Recorder of Deeds, 411 Jules Street, Room 103. Phone 816-271-1437. Nothing is recorded after 4:00 p.m., so your title company will usually file on a business day.

faqs.q: Does St. Joseph inspect rental houses?
faqs.a: Yes. The Residential Rental Certification Program began in July 2019 and requires rental units to pass a minimum code inspection every five years, with a $50.00 fee for each city inspection.

faqs.q: Which school district serves most of St. Joseph?
faqs.a: The St. Joseph School District, which has Benton, Central and Lafayette high schools. A small piece of the city is in the Mid-Buchanan County R-V district.

faqs.q: Can I sell a St. Joseph house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. You can list it, sell it yourself, or sell as-is to a cash buyer. If it is a rental, ask the Housing Compliance Inspection Office at City Hall about its certification status.
